nodes.label: Operator
nodes.description: The local developer who launches the es-view server (npx event-storming-recovery view). At boot they may point it at a model (--model), a traces dir (--traces), or nothing at all, and they read the resolution banner to know which model the session actually ended up serving.

nodes.label: ResolveModel
nodes.description: Decide WHICH Event Storming model the es-view session will serve, from whatever the operator supplied (or nothing), and load it into memory. Applies a fixed 4-tier precedence, then derives a repoRoot for resolving source anchors. This is the single choke point that turns CLI options + the filesystem into the one model the server, API, and MCP all expose.

tactical.explanation: resolveModel({ modelPath, tracesDir, repoRoot, cwd, packageRoot }) applies precedence highest-first: (1) --model <flows.json>: resolve against cwd and readModelFile it (source='model'); (2) --traces <dir>: resolve the dir and call mergeTracesDir to merge the per-flow traces on the fly (source='traces') -- on any validation error it THROWS so the server never serves an invalid model; (3) auto-discover: findFlowsFiles does a bounded recursive walk of cwd (maxDepth 6, skipping node_modules/.git/.claude/dist/.next/out/coverage and any dotdir), sorts hits (a file inside a model/ dir first, then shallower paths, then alphabetical) and reads hits[0] (source='discovered'), pushing a warning when >1 candidate exists; (4) fallback: read the bundled self-model at examples/event-storming-recovery/model/flows.json (source='example'). readModelFile JSON.parses the file and asserts nodes[] and flows[] are arrays (the load-path shape guard). Finally derives resolvedRepoRoot: explicit --repo-root flag > (example fallback -> packageRoot) > model.meta.repoRoot > cwd. Returns { model, source, sourcePath, repoRoot, warnings }. Pure selection/loading; the --traces branch is the only tier that runs the full merge validation.

anchors.note: entry: 4-tier precedence dispatcher
tier 1 --model: readModelFile explicit path
tier 2 --traces: mergeTracesDir + throw on merged.errors
tier 3 auto-discover: findFlowsFiles + hits[0] + multi-candidate warning
tier 4 fallback: bundled example flows.json
bounded recursive walk (maxDepth 6, IGNORE_DIRS + dotdirs)
candidate sort heuristic: model/ dir > shallower > alphabetical
repoRoot derivation: flag > example->packageRoot > meta.repoRoot > cwd

nodes.label: Server Session
nodes.description: One running es-view node process: the resolved model plus the shared in-memory state, serving the SPA, the JSON API, and the MCP endpoint on a single port. Boot-time resolution constitutes the session -- it fixes exactly which model this session serves and the repoRoot used to deep-link anchors back to source. MED confidence: partly infrastructure, but its identity (which model + repoRoot it exposes) is a domain-significant boundary because a connected Claude session reads whatever this session resolved.

tactical.explanation: bin/es-view.mjs main() parses args, calls resolveModel to get { model, source, sourcePath, repoRoot, warnings }, builds the shared services (buildServices: model + indexes + repoRoot + comment store) and the shared in-memory state, then startServer binds the first free port and serves /api/model, /api/selection, /api/context, /api/source and /mcp off that one resolved model. On a resolveModel throw the process prints the error and exits 1 (no session comes up).

anchors.note: session boot: parse args -> resolveModel -> startServer
resolveModel call that constitutes the session's model
model + indexes + repoRoot bundled for API and MCP
/api/model serves the resolved model + provenance

nodes.label: A loaded model file must expose nodes[] and flows[] arrays
nodes.description: ERROR-level load guard: every model read from disk (tiers 1/3/4 -- explicit --model, auto-discovered, and the bundled example) must JSON.parse and carry Array nodes and Array flows, else readModelFile throws and the session refuses to boot (es-view catches and exits 1). This is the ONLY validation those three tiers run: they bypass the full merge invariants, which only the --traces tier enforces. So a structurally-shaped but semantically-invalid flows.json (dangling refs, an aggregate that issues a command, etc.) passes this guard and is served unchecked.

tactical.explanation: readModelFile does JSON.parse(readFileSync(file)) then `if (!model || !Array.isArray(model.nodes) || !Array.isArray(model.flows)) throw`. It runs on the --model, discovered, and example branches (each calls readModelFile) but NOT on --traces, which instead goes through mergeTracesDir/mergeTraceDocs and its invariant suite. bin/es-view.mjs wraps resolveModel in try/catch and process.exit(1) on throw.

anchors.note: JSON.parse the model file
throw unless nodes[] and flows[] are arrays
catch resolveModel throw -> exit 1, no session

nodes.label: ModelResolved
nodes.description: The session has selected and loaded exactly one model and stamped it with provenance: a source tag (one of model | traces | discovered | example), the sourcePath it came from, the warnings gathered along the way, and a derived repoRoot for source anchors. This fact is what every later request (SPA, API, MCP) is answered against.

tactical.explanation: resolveModel returns { model, source, sourcePath, repoRoot, warnings }. `source` records which of the four tiers won; `warnings` carries any multi-candidate discovery note; `repoRoot` is the anchor base. Realized once, at boot, and then frozen for the life of the process. On the --traces tier this fact only holds after the merge validated cleanly (otherwise resolveModel threw before returning).

anchors.note: return { model, source, sourcePath, repoRoot, warnings }

nodes.label: Resolution provenance banner
nodes.description: What the operator reads to know WHERE the served model came from and whether to trust or redirect it: the console banner es-view prints at boot (a human-readable source label, the from-path, the repo-root, the flow/node/hotspot counts, and any warnings) and the same provenance echoed on /api/model's meta. This is how the operator catches 'it served the wrong flows.json' or 'it fell back to the bundled example because nothing was found here'.

tactical.explanation: es-view.mjs prints `model: <SOURCE_LABEL[source]>`, `from: <rel-or-abs sourcePath>`, `repo-root: <repoRoot>`, `contents: N flows, M nodes, K hotspots`, then one `! <warning>` line per resolved.warnings entry. The server also exposes { source, sourcePath, repoRoot, warnings } under /api/model's meta so the SPA can show the same provenance.

anchors.note: banner: model/from/repo-root/contents + per-warning lines
human labels for each source tier
/api/model meta echoes source/sourcePath/repoRoot/warnings

nodes.label: The Model
nodes.description: The canonical Event Storming model (flows.json): deduped nodes plus flows, hotspots, terms, and derived meta. Here it is the thing being resolved -- loaded from disk (tiers 1/3/4) or produced by the on-the-fly merge (tier 2) -- and then held in memory and served for the life of the session. Its invariant boundary is the merge validation in mergeTraceDocs.

tactical.explanation: On the load tiers, agg-model's state is JSON.parsed straight out of a flows.json file by readModelFile. On the --traces tier it is assembled by mergeTraceDocs. Either way resolveModel hands the same in-memory model to buildServices, which indexes it for the API and MCP.

anchors.note: model loaded from a flows.json file (load tiers)
model assembled by the merge (--traces tier)

nodes.label: MergeTraces
nodes.description: Fold every per-flow trace document into one canonical, validated model. Invoked in-process by ResolveModel's --traces tier (merge-on-the-fly) instead of via the es-merge CLI; resolveModel throws if the merge reports any validation error, so the session never serves an invalid merged model.

tactical.explanation: resolveModel's tier-2 branch calls mergeTracesDir(sourcePath), spreads merged.warnings into the resolution warnings, and throws (attaching merged as err.validation) when merged.errors.length > 0. See the merge-traces flow for the full ETL/validation detail.

anchors.note: read dir, parse *.json, delegate to mergeTraceDocs
in-memory --traces call; throws on any validation error

nodes.label: Local filesystem
nodes.description: The local filesystem outside the process, reached through node:fs. ResolveModel reads it three ways: readFileSync of an explicit/discovered/example flows.json, and readdirSync during the bounded recursive auto-discovery walk of the cwd tree.

tactical.explanation: findFlowsFiles walks the tree with fs.readdirSync(withFileTypes) collecting files named flows.json; readModelFile does fs.readFileSync on the chosen file.

anchors.note: readdirSync walk of the cwd subtree

nodes.label: flows.json (canonical model)
nodes.description: A canonical model file on disk. ResolveModel READS it on the --model tier (an explicit path) and the discovered tier (the winning hits[0] from the auto-discovery walk). This is the same file the es-merge CLI writes as output; here it is consumed as input.

tactical.explanation: readModelFile(fs.readFileSync) parses this file on the --model and discovered tiers. On --traces the model is held in memory and this file is never touched.

anchors.note: discovered tier reads hits[0] flows.json

nodes.label: bundled self-model flows.json
nodes.description: The tool's own recovered self-model shipped inside the package at examples/event-storming-recovery/model/flows.json. It is the tier-4 fallback ResolveModel reads when no --model, no --traces, and no auto-discovered flows.json is found, so es-view always has something to show.

tactical.explanation: resolveModel builds the path as path.join(packageRoot, 'examples', 'event-storming-recovery', 'model', 'flows.json') and readModelFiles it; source is tagged 'example' and repoRoot is set to packageRoot (so the example's anchors point at the package's own src/ and tools/).

anchors.note: packageRoot/examples/.../model/flows.json fallback

flows.name: es-view resolves which model the session serves
flows.summary: At boot, es-view must decide which Event Storming model this session will serve. ResolveModel applies a fixed 4-tier precedence -- explicit --model wins, else --traces merges the per-flow traces on the fly (and refuses to serve if that merge fails validation), else it auto-discovers a flows.json by a bounded recursive walk of the current directory, else it falls back to the bundled self-model shipped in the package. It loads the chosen model into memory, tags it with provenance, derives a repoRoot for deep-linking source anchors, and prints a banner so the operator can see which tier won. The recovered intent is 'always come up with SOME model, but make the source unambiguous to the human', with the --traces tier the only one that runs full merge validation.
flows.trigger: Operator runs `npx event-storming-recovery view [--model|--traces|...]`; bin/es-view.mjs main() calls resolveModel at boot.

hotspots.label: Auto-discovery silently picks one flows.json among many
hotspots.description: When no --model/--traces is given and the cwd subtree contains more than one flows.json, ResolveModel serves hits[0] chosen purely by a heuristic sort (a file inside a model/ dir wins, then the shallowest path, then alphabetical) and only emits a warning line -- it does not stop or prompt. Human question: is the heuristic the right default, and is a warning enough, or should multiple candidates be a hard error that forces the operator to pass --model? A stale or example flows.json left in a subdirectory can quietly win over the intended one.

tactical.explanation: findFlowsFiles walks cwd (maxDepth 6) and sorts: model/flows.json first (regex on the path), then fewer path segments, then localeCompare. resolveModel takes discovered[0] and, only when discovered.length > 1, pushes `found N flows.json files; using <rel>. Pass --model to choose another.` into warnings. The selection is otherwise silent and non-blocking.

anchors.note: sort heuristic that decides the winner
take discovered[0]; warn only when >1 candidate

hotspots.label: Derived repoRoot can point at a path that doesn't exist here
hotspots.description: The repoRoot used to resolve every /api/source anchor deep-link is derived, not verified. When no --repo-root flag is passed and the source is a loaded flows.json, repoRoot = model.meta.repoRoot || cwd. The merge NEVER sets meta.repoRoot, so a --traces or freshly merged model falls back to cwd; but a hand-authored or generator-stamped flows.json can carry an absolute meta.repoRoot from the machine that produced it, making anchors resolve against a directory that doesn't exist on this machine (source lookups then fail). Human question: should es-view validate that the derived repoRoot exists / contains the anchored files, and warn or fall back to cwd when it doesn't?

tactical.explanation: resolveModel: resolvedRepoRoot = repoRoot flag ? resolve(cwd,flag) : source==='example' ? packageRoot : (model.meta && model.meta.repoRoot) || cwd. mergeTraceDocs builds meta = { generatedFrom, counts, deadFlows, sharedGlossary } with NO repoRoot key, so merged models always land on cwd; only a pre-existing flows.json with a meta.repoRoot (e.g. an absolute path baked in elsewhere) diverges. No existence check is done on the result.

anchors.note: repoRoot derivation chain, unvalidated
meta built WITHOUT a repoRoot key

hotspots.label: Only --traces validates; --model/discovered/example are served unchecked
hotspots.description: Three of the four tiers (--model, auto-discovered, bundled example) load via readModelFile, whose ONLY check is that nodes[] and flows[] are arrays. They completely bypass the merge's invariant suite (referential integrity, ES grammar, term contract, data lineage). So a structurally-shaped but semantically-broken flows.json -- including one that es-merge itself wrote to disk despite failing validation (see hot-invalid-model-written) and that auto-discovery later picks up -- is served without complaint, while the same content passed via --traces would be rejected. Human question: should the load tiers also run the merge validation (or at least a referential-integrity pass) before serving, so the two entry paths agree?

tactical.explanation: readModelFile does JSON.parse + Array.isArray(nodes)/Array.isArray(flows) only. The --traces tier alone routes through mergeTracesDir/mergeTraceDocs and throws on merged.errors. This mirrors, on the read side, the CLI's write-before-validate gap: es-merge can leave an invalid flows.json on disk, and the discovered tier would serve it after only the shape check.

anchors.note: sole check on load tiers: nodes/flows are arrays
only --traces runs full merge validation (throws on error)
